description: The mathematics of change. Covers limits, derivatives, integrals, and their applications — from rates of change and optimization to area, volume, and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.

concepts.title: Formal Definition of a Limit
learning_objectives: State the epsilon-delta definition of a limit
Construct epsilon-delta proofs for linear and simple polynomial functions
Explain why the formal definition is needed beyond intuitive limit evaluation

concepts.title: Limit Laws and Techniques
learning_objectives: Apply limit laws to evaluate limits of combined functions
Evaluate limits involving absolute value and piecewise functions
Apply the Squeeze Theorem to evaluate limits

concepts.title: Continuity and the Intermediate Value Theorem
learning_objectives: Classify discontinuities as removable, jump, or infinite
Determine continuity of composite and piecewise functions
Apply the Intermediate Value Theorem to guarantee existence of roots

concepts.title: Limits Involving Infinity
learning_objectives: Evaluate limits as x approaches infinity for rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions
Identify vertical and horizontal asymptotes using limits
Evaluate limits of indeterminate forms 0/0 and ∞/∞ (preview of L'Hopital's Rule)

concepts.title: Definition of the Derivative
learning_objectives: Define the derivative as the limit of the difference quotient
Compute derivatives from the limit definition for polynomial and simple radical functions
Interpret the derivative as the instantaneous rate of change and the slope of the tangent line

concepts.title: Differentiability and Continuity
learning_objectives: Determine whether a function is differentiable at a point
Explain why differentiability implies continuity but not the converse
Identify points where a function fails to be differentiable (corners, cusps, vertical tangents)

concepts.title: Basic Differentiation Rules
learning_objectives: Apply the power rule, constant rule, and constant multiple rule
Differentiate sums and differences of functions
Differentiate polynomial and simple radical functions efficiently

concepts.title: Rates of Change in Context
learning_objectives: Interpret the derivative in applied contexts (velocity, marginal cost, growth rate)
Distinguish between average and instantaneous rates of change
Use units to verify and interpret derivative calculations

concepts.title: Product and Quotient Rules
learning_objectives: Derive and apply the product rule for differentiation
Derive and apply the quotient rule for differentiation
Differentiate functions requiring both product and quotient rules

concepts.title: Derivatives of Trigonometric Functions
learning_objectives: Prove that lim(sin x / x) = 1 as x → 0 using the Squeeze Theorem
Differentiate all six trigonometric functions
Apply differentiation rules to expressions involving trigonometric functions

concepts.title: The Chain Rule
learning_objectives: State and apply the chain rule for composite functions
Differentiate nested compositions requiring multiple applications of the chain rule
Combine the chain rule with product, quotient, and trigonometric differentiation rules

concepts.title: Implicit Differentiation
learning_objectives: Differentiate implicitly defined relations with respect to x
Find the slope of the tangent line to an implicitly defined curve at a given point
Apply implicit differentiation to equations involving trigonometric and exponential functions

concepts.title: Derivatives of Inverse Functions
learning_objectives: Derive the formula for the derivative of an inverse function
Differentiate inverse trigonometric functions (arcsin, arccos, arctan)
Apply these derivatives in combination with other differentiation rules

concepts.title: Derivatives of Exponential Functions
learning_objectives: Prove that d/dx[eˣ] = eˣ from the limit definition
Differentiate functions of the form aˣ and e^{g(x)} using the chain rule
Apply exponential derivatives to growth and decay models

concepts.title: Derivatives of Logarithmic Functions
learning_objectives: Differentiate ln x and log_a x
Apply logarithmic differentiation to products, quotients, and powers
Differentiate functions of the form [f(x)]^{g(x)} using logarithmic differentiation

concepts.title: Related Rates
learning_objectives: Set up related rates problems by identifying relationships between varying quantities
Apply implicit differentiation with respect to time to relate rates
Solve classic related rates problems (expanding circles, ladder, conical tank)

concepts.title: Linear Approximation and Differentials
learning_objectives: Compute the linearization of a function at a point
Use linear approximation to estimate function values near a known point
Define differentials dx and dy and use them to estimate error propagation

concepts.title: L'Hopital's Rule
learning_objectives: Apply L'Hopital's Rule to indeterminate forms 0/0 and ∞/∞
Convert indeterminate forms 0·∞, ∞ − ∞, 0⁰, 1^∞, ∞⁰ to apply L'Hopital's Rule
Recognize when L'Hopital's Rule does not apply or leads to circular reasoning

concepts.title: Extreme Values and Critical Points
learning_objectives: State and apply the Extreme Value Theorem
Find critical points by setting the derivative equal to zero or identifying where it is undefined
Find absolute extrema on a closed interval using the Candidates Test

concepts.title: The Mean Value Theorem
learning_objectives: State the Mean Value Theorem and its hypothesis
Find the value c guaranteed by the Mean Value Theorem
Apply Rolle's Theorem as a special case of the Mean Value Theorem

concepts.title: First and Second Derivative Tests
learning_objectives: Apply the first derivative test to classify critical points as local maxima, minima, or neither
Determine intervals of increase and decrease using the first derivative
Apply the second derivative test to classify critical points and determine concavity

concepts.title: Curve Sketching
learning_objectives: Sketch the graph of a function using intercepts, asymptotes, intervals of increase/decrease, concavity, and inflection points
Identify and label all key features on a curve sketch
Relate the graphs of f, f', and f'' to each other

concepts.title: Optimization Problems
learning_objectives: Set up an optimization problem by expressing the objective function in terms of one variable
Apply the closed interval method or first/second derivative test to find optimal values
Solve classic optimization problems (maximum area, minimum distance, minimum cost)

concepts.title: Antiderivatives
learning_objectives: Find general antiderivatives of polynomial, trigonometric, and exponential functions
Apply initial conditions to find particular antiderivatives
Relate antiderivatives to indefinite integrals and the +C convention

concepts.title: Area Under a Curve and Riemann Sums
learning_objectives: Approximate area under a curve using left, right, and midpoint Riemann sums
Express the exact area as the limit of a Riemann sum as n → ∞
Interpret sigma notation in the context of Riemann sums

concepts.title: The Definite Integral
learning_objectives: Define the definite integral as the limit of Riemann sums
Apply properties of definite integrals (linearity, additivity, order)
Evaluate definite integrals using geometry when the integrand has a simple shape

concepts.title: FTC Part 1: Derivatives of Integrals
learning_objectives: State the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus Part 1
Differentiate integral functions of the form F(x) = ∫[a to x] f(t) dt
Apply FTC Part 1 with variable upper limits requiring the chain rule

concepts.title: FTC Part 2: Evaluation of Definite Integrals
learning_objectives: State the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus Part 2
Evaluate definite integrals using antiderivatives
Compute net area and total area using definite integrals

concepts.title: Net Change and the Integral
learning_objectives: Interpret the definite integral as net change (displacement, total growth, accumulated quantity)
Distinguish between displacement and total distance traveled
Apply the net change theorem to real-world rate functions

concepts.title: U-Substitution
learning_objectives: Apply u-substitution to evaluate indefinite and definite integrals
Choose an effective substitution by identifying the inner function of a composition
Adjust limits of integration when applying substitution to definite integrals

concepts.title: Integration by Parts
learning_objectives: Derive integration by parts from the product rule
Apply integration by parts using the LIATE guideline for choosing u and dv
Handle repeated integration by parts and tabular integration

concepts.title: Trigonometric Integrals
learning_objectives: Evaluate integrals of products of sine and cosine using reduction strategies
Evaluate integrals involving powers of tangent and secant
Apply half-angle and power-reducing identities to integration

concepts.title: Trigonometric Substitution
learning_objectives: Identify when to use x = a sin θ, x = a tan θ, or x = a sec θ substitutions
Evaluate integrals involving √(a² − x²), √(a² + x²), and √(x² − a²)
Convert back to the original variable using right-triangle diagrams

concepts.title: Partial Fraction Decomposition
learning_objectives: Decompose a proper rational function into partial fractions with linear and irreducible quadratic factors
Handle repeated factors in partial fraction decomposition
Integrate rational functions using partial fractions

concepts.title: Improper Integrals
learning_objectives: Evaluate improper integrals with infinite limits of integration
Evaluate improper integrals with integrand discontinuities
Determine whether an improper integral converges or diverges using direct evaluation and comparison

concepts.title: Numerical Integration
learning_objectives: Approximate definite integrals using the Trapezoidal Rule
Approximate definite integrals using Simpson's Rule
Estimate the error bound for numerical integration methods

concepts.title: Area Between Curves
learning_objectives: Set up and evaluate integrals for the area between two curves
Determine the appropriate variable of integration (dx or dy) for area problems
Handle regions requiring multiple integrals due to crossing curves

concepts.title: Volumes by Disks and Washers
learning_objectives: Derive and apply the disk method for volumes of revolution about the x-axis and y-axis
Derive and apply the washer method when a region is revolved about an axis
Set up volume integrals for revolution about lines other than the coordinate axes

concepts.title: Volumes by Cylindrical Shells
learning_objectives: Derive and apply the shell method for volumes of revolution
Choose between disk/washer and shell methods based on the geometry of the region
Set up shell integrals for revolution about vertical and horizontal axes

concepts.title: Volumes by Cross-Sectional Area
learning_objectives: Compute volumes of solids with known cross-sectional shapes (squares, triangles, semicircles)
Set up the integral for volume as the integral of cross-sectional area
Visualize three-dimensional solids from two-dimensional cross-section descriptions

concepts.title: Arc Length
learning_objectives: Derive the arc length formula from the distance formula and limits
Compute arc length of a curve y = f(x) over an interval
Set up arc length integrals for parametrically defined curves

concepts.title: Surface Area of Revolution
learning_objectives: Derive the formula for surface area of a solid of revolution
Compute the surface area generated by revolving a curve about the x-axis or y-axis
Evaluate or set up surface area integrals for given curves

concepts.title: Work and Fluid Force
learning_objectives: Calculate work done by a variable force as a definite integral
Solve spring, pumping, and lifting problems using integration
Calculate fluid pressure and fluid force on a submerged surface

concepts.title: Center of Mass and Moments
learning_objectives: Compute the centroid of a planar region using integration
Apply the moment formulas Mx and My for a lamina of uniform density
Apply Pappus' theorem to find volumes and surface areas of revolution

concepts.title: Sequences and Their Limits
learning_objectives: Determine convergence or divergence of a sequence from its formula
Apply the Monotone Convergence Theorem for bounded monotonic sequences
Compute limits of sequences using algebraic techniques and L'Hopital's Rule

concepts.title: Infinite Series and Convergence Tests
learning_objectives: Define partial sums and determine convergence of a series from its partial sum sequence
Apply the divergence test, integral test, and p-series test
Apply the comparison test and limit comparison test

concepts.title: Alternating Series and Absolute Convergence
learning_objectives: Apply the alternating series test and estimate the remainder
Distinguish between absolute and conditional convergence
Apply the ratio test and root test for absolute convergence

concepts.title: Power Series and Radius of Convergence
learning_objectives: Define a power series centered at a point
Determine the radius and interval of convergence using the ratio or root test
Check convergence at the endpoints of the interval

concepts.title: Taylor and Maclaurin Series
learning_objectives: Derive the Taylor series of a function centered at a given point
Write Maclaurin series for eˣ, sin x, cos x, and 1/(1−x)
Use known series to derive new series by substitution, differentiation, or integration

concepts.title: Taylor Polynomials and Remainder Estimation
learning_objectives: Approximate a function with its nth-degree Taylor polynomial
Apply Taylor's inequality (Lagrange remainder) to bound the error of approximation
Determine how many terms are needed for a desired accuracy

concepts.title: Applications of Power Series
learning_objectives: Use power series to evaluate integrals that have no closed-form antiderivative
Use power series to solve limits and differential equations
Represent special functions (Bessel functions preview) as power series

projects.title: The Brachistochrone Problem
projects.description: Investigate the curve of fastest descent between two points. Set up the time integral using arc length and energy conservation, then compare the cycloid solution to straight-line and circular arc paths numerically.
learning_objectives: Formulate a physical optimization problem as a calculus problem
Set up and evaluate arc length and time-of-travel integrals
Compare numerical results from different curve choices

projects.title: Building a Numerical Integrator
projects.description: Implement the trapezoidal rule, Simpson's rule, and Riemann sums from scratch. Test on functions with known antiderivatives and analyze convergence rates.
learning_objectives: Translate mathematical formulas into algorithmic procedures
Measure and compare the convergence rate of different integration methods
Analyze error behavior as the number of subintervals increases

projects.title: Computing π with Infinite Series
projects.description: Explore three different series representations of π (Leibniz, Nilakantha, Machin's formula). Prove convergence, compute partial sums, and compare convergence rates.
learning_objectives: Derive series representations of π from Taylor series of arctan
Compare convergence rates of different series for the same value
Apply remainder estimates to determine terms needed for a desired precision
